mainAirport.name: Hobart International Airport
mainAirport.notes: Single runway 12/30, 2,727 m (extended 2017-18; strengthened/widened for A350/787 in 2024-25, reopened Aug 2025). Traffic is mostly A320/737 and turboprops; no regular wide-body services yet (Air New Zealand to Auckland uses narrow-bodies; Antarctic and freight flights occasional). Runway-end coordinates are from SkyVector (0.01-minute precision, ~20 m); the runway 12 end has a ~120 m displaced threshold, so ends[0] is the physical runway end, slightly north-west of the landing threshold. Flight path changes in 2022 drew complaints (Aircraft Noise Ombudsman investigation) in suburbs such as Seven Mile Beach, Lewisham and the eastern shore.

otherAirports.name: Cambridge Aerodrome
otherAirports.note: Small general-aviation field about 3 km west of Hobart Airport: Par Avion scenic flights, the aero club's training aircraft and helicopters. Put up for sale in June 2024; homes in Cambridge and Seven Mile Beach hear light aircraft and helicopters. Runway ends are APPROXIMATE (placed from the reference point, runway length ~1,100-1,200 m and magnetic headings plus ~15.5 deg variation), not surveyed.

plans.name: Northern Suburbs Rapid Bus (Northern Suburbs Transit Corridor)
plans.status: Planning; public consultation closes 9 Oct 2026, no build date yet
plans.about: Rapid bus between the city and Claremont every 10 min at peak, partly on the unused northern rail corridor, with 12 stops including New Town, Moonah, Glenorchy and Berriedale. Light rail options have faded in favour of bus rapid transit.

plans.name: New Bridgewater Bridge
plans.about: $786m four-lane bridge over the Derwent between Granton and Bridgewater replacing the 1946 lift bridge, part of the Midland Highway. Faster trips from Brighton/Bridgewater into Hobart.

plans.name: Southern Outlet transit lane (fifth lane)
plans.status: Partly built; Davey-Macquarie connector done, main lane unfunded/undated (costs up to $95m, 2026)
plans.about: A fifth, bus/transit lane on the Southern Outlet between Tolmans Hill and the city to ease Kingston commuter congestion. The southern section to Kingston is not yet designed.

plans.name: Tasman Highway: Midway Point and Sorell causeways duplication
plans.status: Design and environmental approvals (2026); no construction date
plans.about: $187m to widen the causeways between Hobart Airport and Sorell to four lanes, add a second McGees Bridge and raise the road for flooding. Part of the $350m South East Traffic Solution.

mainAirport.name: Canberra Airport
mainAirport.curfew: No curfew (24/7); noise abatement areas keep jets at 5,000 ft+ over most suburbs
mainAirport.notes: Main runway 17/35 is 2,983 m; 12/30 is 1,679 m. Mostly A320/737/E190 domestic jets plus turboprops and RAAF VIP/defence aircraft (Fairbairn); international is narrow-body (e.g. Bali, Fiji) with no regular wide-body passenger service. Since 1996 noise abatement areas require jets to stay at least 5,000 ft (others 3,000 ft) above most of Canberra, which the airport says protects 99.5% of houses from direct overflight; traffic funnels over the Majura valley, Queanbeyan/Jerrabomberra and Hume/Tuggeranong-east. Airport says night freight and international flying will grow. Coordinates from SkyVector (0.01-minute precision); runway 35 has a ~300 m displaced threshold and 30 a ~65 m one, so those ends are physical runway ends. Airservices WebTrak shows live tracks.

mainAirport.name: Darwin International Airport / RAAF Base Darwin
mainAirport.notes: Joint-user airport: civil flights share the runways with RAAF Base Darwin. Main runway 11/29 is 3,354 m; 18/36 is 1,524 m. Airline traffic is mostly 737/A320/A220/turboprops (few scheduled wide-bodies), but military heavies (KC-30A/A330, C-17, P-8, visiting US tankers and transports) are regular, and fighters (F-35A, F/A-18, visiting foreign jets during Exercise Pitch Black in odd years) are by far the loudest events. The airport sits in the middle of the northern suburbs, so Ludmilla, Coconut Grove, Nightcliff, Marrara, Jingili, Millner, Karama and Berrimah are close to the runway ends. Defence publishes the 2043 ANEF (Sep 2023) covering RAAF Base Darwin, Darwin Airport and Robertson Barracks (army helicopters). B-52 bomber facilities and rotations are at RAAF Base Tindal near Katherine, ~300 km away, not Darwin, though US force posture works (e.g. USAF mission planning centre, fuel and apron works) also affect Darwin. Coordinates from SkyVector (0.01-minute precision).

future.label: Defence and airline growth to 2043 (2043 ANEF)
future.explain: Defence's 2043 ANEF for RAAF Base Darwin and Darwin Airport models growing civil and military flying (including new fighter types and allied activity) out to 2043. Check a home against those forecast contours rather than today's noise, especially near the 11/29 runway ends.

plans.about: Proposed gas, minerals-processing and renewables industrial precinct on the Middle Arm peninsula across the harbour from Palmerston. Controversial; still in assessment.
